title: Public and Population Health Informatics: The Bridging of Big Data to Benefit Communities
abstract:
Summary

Objective:  To summarize the recent public and population health informatics literature with a focus on the synergistic “bridging” of electronic data to benefit communities and other populations.

Methods:  The review was primarily driven by a search of the literature from July 1, 2016 to September 30, 2017. The search included articles indexed in PubMed using subject headings with (MeSH) keywords “public health informatics” and “social determinants of health”. The “social determinants of health” search was refined to include articles that contained the keywords “public health”, “population health” or “surveillance”.

Results:  Several categories were observed in the review focusing on public health's socio-technical infrastructure: evaluation of surveillance practices, surveillance methods, interoperable health information infrastructure, mobile health, social media, and population health. Common trends discussing socio-technical infrastructure included big data platforms, social determinants of health, geographical information systems, novel data sources, and new visualization techniques. A common thread connected these categories of workforce, governance, and sustainability: using clinical resources and data to bridge public and population health.

Conclusions:  Both medical care providers and public health agencies are increasingly using informatics and big data tools to create and share digital information. The intent of this “bridging” is to proactively identify, monitor, and improve a range of medical, environmental, and social factors relevant to the health of communities. These efforts show a significant growth in a range of population health-centric information exchange and analytics activities.
author: Gamache, Roland;Kharrazi, Hadi;Weiner, Jonathan P.;

title: Computer assisted classroom discussion in three ESL classrooms : a case study of the experiences of a teacher and her students
abstract: The purpose of this study was to examine the experiences of an ESL teacher and her students in computer assisted classroom discussion (CACD) and how these experiences were shaped and constructed. Thirty-four ESL students from two listening/speaking classes and one writing class enrolled in the English Language Program (ELP) affiliated with a large university in the U.S. and a teacher of those three classes participated. Main data sources included interviews with every student and the teacher, observation notes both in the classroom and in the computer lab, and transcripts from the weekly CACD sessions. The results of study indicated that 1) students' individual differences (typing skills, English language proficiency, pre-conceived beliefs about language learning and learning in general, and perceptions of the CACD); 2) the nature of the CACD (its fast pace, multiple voices and information overload, students' empowerment, and written communication); 3) the language of the CACD (off-topic and abusive messages, low quality language input, lack of error correction); and 4) social factors in the CACD (group dynamics, responsiveness, and tension among Korean participants) considerably influenced students' experiences in the CACD. In addition, four major themes that fashioned the teacher's experiences in the CACD were identified: 1) limited resources, 2) the teacher's goals for the class and the CACD, 3) the teacher's roles in implementing and participating in the CACD, and 4) the influence of the students' messages in the CACD. Further analysis revealed that students' experiences in the CACD that were influenced by those numerous factors contributed considerably to constructing students' beliefs about the use of CACD in language learning. One of the critical factors that led many students to their negative beliefs about the use of CACD in language learning was their pre-conceived beliefs about language learning and learning in general. It was also found that students' empowerment could be perceived differently according to their cultural backgrounds, and that some of the factors, especially abusive discourses, group dynamics, knowledge of relevant skills such as language proficiency and typing skills, and social identity of Korean students established power structures within CACD that sometimes constrained students' empowerment.

title: 우리나라 지방정부의 지역축제 평가시스템에 관한연구
abstract: After the execution of the Local Autonomy system each local governments of the Republic of Korea recognized the festival as one important means of local development and unity and through this they are devotion efforts and various trals such as revitalizing the local economy and establishing local identity. Festival is understood as an universal socio-cultural phenomenon that exists in every region and every time and also understood as a general expression which represents local culture and play together with an initiation ceremony, history of the region, event and religion. Many big and small festivals are being held numerously every year around us and its large ripple effect has been a big stepping - stone to the growth of the local society. But various forms of opposite function together with these pure function began to surface and also the critical view on festival si largely increasing. Search for new way of development on festival with technical analysis and evaluation system on the due problems must be required. Central government or each local autonomy organizations have their own evaluation system on festival but festivals are planned based on one purpose and evaluation rather than different value and standard which occurred lack of identity and diversity. Therefore, introduction of rational and objective evaluation indicator is required which can be the right standard for each characteristic and type of the festival. Under such awareness of the problem, in this study we will observe how and in what forms the national festivals are held especially focusing on how local festival is evaluated by the evaluation system and supported. To achieve the purpose of this study, we closely analyzed the evaluation system on Culture &Tourism festival carried out by the local government then found problems of the current evaluation system have and suggested an alternative idea. As a consequence, we discovered several characteristics as below. First, most of the past and present evaluation on festival are based on the festival evaluation system of the ministry of culture &Tourism. But the evaluation system on the culture &tourism festival aims to promote 'the culture &tourism festival'. This is not a general evaluation on local festival but to promote the well - known local tourism festival such as making international images or inviting foreign tourists. Although various culture &tourism festivals are planned and carried out successfully, the truth is there are many problems occurred as the influence of these evaluation system increases. Second, to evaluate the culture &tourism festival assigned by the Ministry of Culture &Tourism multilaterally and for the strict evaluation, there is an effort to evaluate by understanding not only the visual characteristic but also the characteristic of the organization and project of the festival. Although the culture &tourism festival is an object of the evaluation, evaluation indicator is composed of the items which evaluate the local festival in general so it is quite questionable how precisely they can evaluate the primary purpose of the culture &tourism festival. Third, there is an effort to differentiate the festival evaluation indicator and general character by the purpose of the festival evaluation. Evaluation on the same evaluation system can be different according to the purpose of evaluation. Most of the studies related to the present festival evaluation are evaluations on few individual festivals and the evaluation system of the Ministry of Culture &Tourism is to select festival which mainly aims tourism. An ostensible purpose of the evaluation system of the culture solidarity is an evaluation on the whole local festival trend but the object of the evaluation is mainly culture &tourism festival which evaluation purpose contradicts the evaluation object. Fourth, other countries have various evaluation indicator and evaluation system according to the purpose and characteristic of the festival and especially they mainly focus on the parts which our evaluation system neglects such as evaluation on the influence of festival and how festival affects socio-cultural &psychological factor, connection with other events, problem-solving powers, capacity of the festival manager, holding will of the festival. Local festival evaluation system exercised by the local government has several problems as below. First, although most of the local governments held various types of festival because the problems of the festival's course, each festival has no clear primary purpose, course and creativity that vagueness is found in common about how we should evaluate the festival evaluation with what standard and priority. Second, as we observe the evaluation indicator exercised by the local government, most of the local government's festival evaluation highly focuses on the tourism or economic effect but they should try to evaluate with various evaluation indicator by the purpose of the festival and its content. Third, in case of the evaluation on the socio-cultural ripple effect that many festival evaluation attempts, evaluation subject should be classified as local residents, visitors, outside expert by the course &purpose of the festival and the purpose &virtue of the evaluation but wrong selection of this leaded to the failure of the objective evaluation. Fourth, festival evaluation report is composed of 3 main parts; visitor survey, result survey of inviting foreign tourist and festival visit evaluation. As items of the visitor survey are not unified, they have difference by organizations on the festival evaluation result and this makes the objective and general evaluation difficult. In result survey of inviting foreign tourist, we can find many different points of view on visitor standard such as inconsistent statistics of the visitor between the festival promotion committee and related organization because of the inaccurate standard. In festival visit evaluation, there are many cases that exessive intervention of the festival visitor's subjective opinion hiders the objective evaluation. Effort to develop with the uniformity and universality of the culture &tourism festival evaluation system, to regulate and complement delicately and to evlauate festivals in various category by multilateral view-point is needed. To improve the local festival evaluation system of the local government. First, the local festival evaluation system must establish the development guideline. For this, accurate understanding and evaluation of the increasing local festival's actual condition must be made to improve the quality of the festival and establish the guideline. Second, composition of the local festival evaluation model must be established. To make a desirable model, we must analyze the prosent situation precisely and suggest the upcoming development guideline. We have to establish evaluation model that analyzes the whole process of the festival synthetic and terminable which is the general phenomenon of politics, society, economy and culture. Third, composition of the local festival evaluation character by thetypes of the festival must be conducted. Most of our local government's festival evaluation system indicates the character which evaluates objectively, systematically and generally with no fixed standard and these characters are focused on visitor-oriented evaluation. We must grasp which is the prior character and what character is important. Fourth, multilateral evaluation system by the types of the festival must be established. Evaluation by outside expert on the festival was common until now but multilateral evaluation by the festival related understanding group is relatively rare. Therefore, evaluation of the promoter and outside expert comes out totally different ofr the numerical value o the festival quality is entirely different with the visitor or local resident's impression because the outside expert evaluates with one-sided view. Also, it was hard to get an objective and rational result because of the difficult access to the accurate data. For rational and objective evaluation of thefestival, multilateral evaluation system of the outside expert, promoter, visitor and local resident must be established. Lastly, we must have various evaluation support systems by the types of the festival. For this reason, festival should be categorized by its type, location and characteristic and each category must have different object, guideline and scale of support and we should prevent the native local culture form being degrades as tourism-purposed consuming festival and commercialized. In this study, we analyzed the festival evaluation system of our local government in multilateral view-point, discovered several problems and suggested alternative idea. But this study also has a great limitation. It was difficult to secure the reference data because of the characteristic of this study and his leaded to limited usage and reliance of the data. We failed to enforce positive analysis targeting the festival promoter of each local government and problem discovery &search for alternative idea through this which makes this sturdy more efficient. Study results would be more meaningful fo the study heareafter overcomes the limitations mentioned above.

title: Causal Attributions (Framing)
abstract:
<jats:p>Causal attributions are an element of a frame (Entman, 1991). Furthermore, a causal attribution organizes the anatomy of a problem within a text. Hereby, causal attributions provide explanations of problems in terms of their expectations, the underlying reasons or the causes that led to one or more problems depicted in the text.
Entry connected to 
framing devices
cultural motifs
Field of Application/Theoretical Foundation 
The causal attributions variable is used in both deductive and inductive framework analyses (e.g., Boesman & Van Gorp, 2018; Cools et al., 2024; Van Gorp, 2007, 2010). Frame analyses with a socio-constructionist approach (Van Gorp, 2007) discuss a strong correlation of causal attributions with cultural motifs (Gamson & Modigliani, 1989). However and in the context of journalistic articles in particular, the main aim tends to depict the facts and problems of an event that is being discussed and to be able to understand and solve it. To that, causal attributions are – presumably – more closely linked to the problem definition than to the cultural motifs. In other words, not every problem may be underpinned by a cultural dimension in a press release, but it is far more likely to be underpinned by a causal attribution.
References/Combination with other methods of data collection 
Causal attributions refer to a causal interpretation of an event or an actors’ statement, while also highlighting certain aspects of cultural motifs. This may be a result of “discursive negotiation”.
Example studies: Pentzold & Knorr (2024); Pentzold & Fischer (2017); Van Gorp & Vercruysse (2012)
Information on Van Gorp & Vercruysse, 2012
Authors: Baldwin Van Gorp and Tom Vercruysse
Research questions: What are the dominant frames used to represent dementia and what alternative frames could be proffered?
Object of analysis: An inductive frame analysis to examine the various ways in which the media define dementia both in news aggregates and in audio-visual material from the internet. The aim is to find indications of how and what conceptions people gain of dementia through news, audiovisual material, novels, and public health brochures. Hereby, the analysis followed an initial three-step coding procedure: First, the authors conducted the material inductively by coding key terms, with regular feedback moments to discuss potential divergences. This first phase ended when no new frames were detected, followed by an axial coding procedure of the whole material during phase two. Here, every new passage from the material had to be connected to at least one frame package so to verify the pre-defined frames from phase one. Third and lastly, frame packages were created by linking both reasoning devices and framing devices with a cultural theme.
Time frame of analysis and analyzed media type: The sample consisted of a representative selection of Belgian newspaper coverage from March 1, 2008 to July 1, 2010. In addition, books about dementia (n=20) were examined together with (audio-)visual material (n=14) based on the search results for “dementia” on www.imdb.com and www.youtube.com. Finally, public health brochures of dementia were part of the sample (n=15).
Information about variable 
Variable/name definition: Frames/frame packages that define dementia
Scale: Nominal
Level of analysis: In the beginning by paragraph level, then the whole text as the frames began to emerge more clearly.
Sample operationalization: A frame / frame package consists of seven elements. These are the following: (1) cultural theme; (2) definition of the problem; (3) cause (why is it a problem?); (4) consequences; (5) moral values involved; (6) possible solutions/actions; (7) metaphors, choice of vocabulary.  
Values: The qualitative analysis resulted in a total of twelve frame packages (six frames and six counter-frames). Each consists of a central cultural theme, a definition of dementia, the causes and possible consequences, the moral evaluation and possible future scenarios of dementia. (1A. Dualism of body and mind vs. 1B. Unity of body and mind; 2; The invader; 3. The strange travelling companion; 4A. Faith in science vs. 4B. Natural ageing; 5. The fear of death and degeneration; 6. Carpe diem; 7A. Reversed roles vs. 7B. Each in turn; 8A. No quid pro quo vs. 8B. The Good Mother)
Reliability: First, both authors coded independently of each other and met to discuss differences. This resulted in tentative frames which were used for further qualitative research of the material. Then, the frames found were discussed with experts (in a workshop setting).
Codebook: Description of the sample (newspapers and audiovisual material) can be found at the end of the article (appendix of Van Gorp & Vercruysse, 2012).
Information on Pentzold & Knorr, 2024 
Authors: Christian Pentzold and Charlotte Knorr
Research questions: With which imaginaries do journalistic reports make sense of Big Data? (RQ1) How do these imaginaries evolve over time? (RQ2) To what extent are the imaginaries similar or different across countries? (RQ3)
Object of analysis [and analyzed media type]: The project Framing Big Data (DFG 2021-2024) analyzed the media-communicatively articulated frames on “Big Data” in online newspapers and magazines from three countries: South Africa, Germany, and the United States. No visual material was collected or examined. In total, material from 26 newspapers and magazines was analyzed. The time frame ranged from 2011 to 2020 (N=1,456). Articles had to contain the keywords “big data” or “dataf*” (e.g., datafication, datafied) in the headline, sub-headline and/or first paragraph (sampling criteria).
To analyze the frames manually, it was assumed that frames are organized according to three levels analysable in a press text. First, the reasoning devices, followed by – secondly – the framing devices (references, argumentation patterns, idioms, metaphors, topoi) and – thirdly – the cultural motifs. Coming from a socio-constructionist approach, a cultural motif is the anchor of an idea expressed in a text (Van Gorp, 2010, p. 7). It is connected to a social problem. To understand this connection, the problem definition, causal attribution, treatment recommendation, and moral evaluation associated with the coded cultural motif were analyzed (cf., Van Gorp, 2010, p. 91-92; Entman, 1991, p. 52).  These four elements are the reasoning devices of a frame. They are accompanied by the so-called framing devices which are stylistic devices, catchphrases, metaphors, and references. To that end, for the manual frame analysis on Big Data in the press aggregates, we developed codes for framing devices (1), reasoning devices (2), and cultural motifs (3). All three elements form part of a frame package (Van Gorp, 2007, 2010).
To build the frame packages, we followed procedures of both block modeling and cluster analysis. First, a block modeling was conducted – as introduced by White for structural analyses (White et al., 1976) – to prepare the data set for the cluster analysis. Then, the coded cultural motifs, the reasoning devices, and the framing devices that correlated strongly in the data set (a total of 9 variables and 34 codes) were chosen. With that, a hierarchical cluster analysis (Ward method) was conducted (Matthes & Kohring, 2008, p. 268). Binary variables were calculated for each of the codes of the nine variables.
Time frame of analysis: 2011, Jan 1 – 2020, Dec 31
Codebook: Public_Codebook_FBD_fin.pdf
Information about the variable 
Variable name/definition: Causal Attributions
Scale: Nominal
Level of analysis: Whereas the formal categories in the manual content analysis were coded at the level of a single news item, the individual frame elements were coded at the level of propositional units. A propositional unit (= analysis unit) can be connected to several codes that are assigned to either a framing device, a reasoning device or a cultural motif. Not all but some frame elements had to be present in the news item, and at least one reasoning device. Furthermore, at least one reasoning device should be tied to a framing device and/or cultural motif to prove that the propositional unit contains semantic relationships and not just elements of “raw text” (van Atteveldt, 2008, p. 5). 
Sample operationalization Causal attributions are part of reasoning devices that include a problem definition, a causal attribution, a treatment recommendation, and a moral evaluation. To identify a causal attribution, we asked: What causes, reasons or expectations are associated with big data while others are ignored? How does an articulated cause, reason or expectation shape a concrete problem of big data while hiding others? Either as expectations (following the conviction/hope etc. to …) OR reasons (in order to…) OR as causes (because of …) for big data. (multiple causal attributions can be coded per article; but only one per propositional unit)
Values: see Table 1.
Reliability: α = .669 [Krippendorff’s alpha, intercoder reliability. A total of seven reliability tests were conducted, five of them during the coding phase and two as part of two pretests. Five coders were involved in four tests, four coders were involved in three tests. All tests were conducted in the period July 2022 to December 2022].

title: Analysing the Impact of Education Policies and Their Implementation on the School Education System in Punjab, Pakistan
abstract:
<jats:p>In Punjab, Pakistan, a province whose educational outcomes are pivotal to national development, the school system continues to struggle with significant challenges in access, quality, and equity. Despite a long history of ambitious education policies, a persistent and critical gap exists between policy intentions and their practical implementation, leaving many students without quality learning opportunities and teachers without adequate support. This narrative review analyzes the landscape of education policy and reform since 2001, synthesizing a wide body of evidence from policy documents, peer-reviewed academic research, and government reports to diagnose the root causes of this systemic implementation failure. The findings reveal several interconnected bottlenecks that consistently stall improvement. Chronic policy inconsistency, driven by volatile political cycles, prevents long-term strategies from taking root. Weak monitoring and evaluation systems render it nearly impossible to track progress or make evidence-based adjustments, while deep-seated urban-rural disparities in funding and resources perpetuate cycles of inequality. These issues are compounded by systemic corruption and administrative inefficiency that divert critical funds and erode public trust. Crucially, the review highlights a pervasive lack of meaningful stakeholder engagement in the policy process, which undermines local ownership and the sustainability of reforms. The paper argues that breaking this cycle requires a fundamental shift away from top-down reforms towards more adaptive and participatory strategies. This involves a concerted effort to strengthen policy coherence, invest in teacher capacity through continuous professional development, leverage technology for transparency, and empower communities through participatory monitoring to finally bridge the policy-practice gap.

title: Typological Study On the Workplace Faith Fellowship In Its Three Stages of Historical Development in Korea
abstract: I. INTRODUCTION A. Posing of Problem and the Task of Study The National Statistical Office reported that about 22,219,000 workers are employed nationwide by the September, 2002. This numeric reaches 46.6% of the whole population in Korea. Recent report says that workers feel discouraged and unsecured because of the hostile working environment, limitless competition, structural injustice of industrial society, economic and societal conflict between the rich and the poor, psychological stress and tension, collapse of family and virtue system, and, blurring of the ethical sensitivity in the workplace. It is not surprising therefore to hear from the groups of age in 20' and 30' complaining of their unstable job and future. 'For where two or three are gathered together in my name, I am there in the midst of them' (Mt. 18:20). So many believers have experienced hope and consolation from this text. The text gives not only psychological easiness but also Chris tian vision of vocation that the workplace is the one in which Christ's presence is to be experienced and witnessed. Workplace Faith Fellowship has been the place in which believers are exposed to the concrete real world and encouraged to create and participate in the mystical visible body of Christ, and called to share Christian life in a hostile real world of selfishness, competition, and injustice. It has challenged believers to live with honesty and responsibility the wholistic Christian life supposed to be accomplished through the interconnected structures of family, church, and work place. Considering of its original vision, however, future of the WF appears to be not so hopeful because of the accelerating process of secularization in society. For the writer devoting to the workplace ministry in the Holy Love Church Furniture Company last ten years, current situation is discouraging. How could I revitalize and realize the original vision of the workplace mission? How could I form the faith community in workplace in which believers are challenged to express and create their Christian identity? How could believers be more faithful to Christ's simple words like these: 'Go into all the world and preach the gospel to every creature' (Mark 16:15); 'You are the salt of the earth but if the salt loses its flavor, how shall it be seasoned? It is then good for nothing but to be thrown out and trampled underfoot by men' (Matthew 5:13). Task of the study is to characterize and evaluate the activities and influence of WFs by using four typologies the writer creates, that is, the worship-centered, the Bible study-centered, the mission-centered, and fellowship-centered, from theological and sociological perspectives, with its three stages of historical development in view. Motif of the study is to help members, leaders, prospective leaders of WF and church leadership confronting ones' history and thereby revitalizing their self-identity in a new way. B. Methodology and the Scope of the Study The study depends on literary analysis of diverse materials from WF and visitation. In Introduction, task and motif of the study will be revealed. Scope of study will be defined. In Chapter II, theoretical ground of WF will be laid, historically, theologically, and sociologically. Historical origins of three categories of WF especially in connection with its leadership style be introduced historically. Theological principles or assumptions of WF will be analyzed in terms of the nature of laity, stewardship, and mission of sending. In sociological analysis, the writer will deal with the value of vocation in diverse perspectives. Chapter III, IV and V deal with history of the WF in its three stages of development: the early (1950'-1970'), the middle (1980'-1990'), and the present (2000-present). Activities in each stage will be explored and characterized in four typologies: the worship centered, the Bible study centered, the mission centered, and the fellowship-diakonia centered, evaluated from theological and sociological perspective, and, summarized critically. II. Theoretical Reflection on Workplace Faith Fellowship A. Historical Reflection The writer analyzes the history of Korean WF in four typologies of the worship centered, the Bible Study Centered, mission centered, and fellowship centered. Four typologies are categorized in terms of the primary concerns and focuses of activities of diverse groups of WF. Though not adopted as a categorizing typology in the thesis, another perspective to categorize WFs would be worth being remarked. It is related to the question of leadership, that is, 'who takes initiative to run WF. 1. Independent Workplace Faith Fellowship Historical origin of WF is known to be a prayer meeting held in Dansung Sa (movie theater) run at that time by Byuksan Co. in 1956. Initiative of this meeting was taken by a devote Christian owner of Byuksan Co.. Theater was open to public on Sunday. And Christians of employees in the company couldn't attend Sunday Worship Service. The owner felt deeply sorry about this situation, finally decided to provide certain space and time (one of weekday) for employees to have opportunity to have service. Though not systematically organized and given space for more creative and extended activities compared to WF today, WF in Dansung Sa is a historical phenomena in Korean christian soil in which worship service celebrated in the church on Sunday is the normative considered biblical and therefore effective. Characteristic of this type of WF is that the owner of the company takes initiative and the activities are restricted more or less within that company. 2. Workplace Mission Association In the pluralistic secular city like Seoul, there are so many big companies, officially not affiliated to any religion. It is hard in this case to get any help for Christian activities from companies, for example. Under this circumstance, there comes up individual Christians, forming an areal christian network which could be called WF. Usually they ask churches in area to provide space and sometimes leadership for meeting. The meeting held at Chonkyo Methodist Church in 1979 is the one in this kind. They first called the meeting as 'Thursday workplace church' because they met at Thursday lunchtime. Members of this meeting introduced their activities around the area, invited other Christian workers to the Easter Service in 1980, and decided to develop 'Thursday workplace church' into 'Workplace Mission Association.' This type of WF has been established since then in big cities, now reaching the nationwide networking of 38 areal organizations by now. In this type of WF, leadership or the initiative is taken by christian workers' network voluntarily established, but with strong relationship with one church in the area who provides meeting space, financial support, and some part of leadership. 3. Workplace Church Worship Workplace Church Worship is a type of meeting in which a certain church takes full initiative in making organization, funding, and providing leadership. The meeting usually origins as a result of mission project of an urban church for the area. Youngrak Presbyterian church began this type of mission project September 5 1969. Church invited workers of Ssang Yong Cement, Bbaek general hospital, Jungbu police station and began worship service at lunch time every Friday. In this type of WP, leadership is under a local church. B. Theological Reflection 1. Theology of Laity Theological ground of WF appears to be theology of laity which is based on the doctrine of priesthood of believers reclaimed by Martin Luther. Luther argued that the only mediator is Jesus Christ and christians baptized have grace of privilege to participate in Christ's priesthood as his visible body in this world. This means that every christian has a duty and privilege to proclaim gospel and offer a prayer of intercession in every place and time, offering spiritual and living worship. Priesthood and apostolic right is not just restricted to the church institution (ordained clergy). Priesthood is to be reinterpreted and applied to all believers in Jesus Christ. The doctrine of priesthood of believers is the ground of the theology of laity and theological justification of WF. What is the biblical meaning of the term 'laity'? As 'laos,' in Greek, it indicates people of God including both clergy and believers not ordained. The term 'laity' is a glorious word because people of God is nothing other than a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, God's own people made to proclaim the mighty acts of him who call themselves out of darkness into his marvelous light (1 Peter 2:9). In the early stage of the Christian history, laity means community of believers including apostles, prophets, teachers, deacons, and others given diverse gifts from Holy Spirit, only later, coming to be degraded when it began to indicate a group of believers unordained, passive, derivative and secondary compared to the ordained in the mission of the church. Theology of laity based upon the doctrine of priesthood of believers appears to be implied or assumed in activities of WF. 2. Theology of Stewardship Another theological principle of workplace mission comes from Genesis 1: 28: 'have dominion over the fish of the sea and over the bird....' Message is about stewardship assigned and commanded to human being as image of God. Steward is the faithful and prudent manager (Luke 12:42), servants of Christ and steward of God's mysteries (1 Cor. 4:1), guardians and trustees, blameless (Gal. 4:2). To serve the world as Christ did is one of theological principles which could explain WF's activities in meaningful way. 3. Theology of 'Being Sent' Jesus Christ trained his disciples for three years, sending them to the world. In John 17:18 reading 'As you have sent me into the world, so I have sent them onto the world,' what we see is the special relationship among God, Jesus Christ and disciples, the relationship characterized as 'sending' and 'sent.' God sent Jesus and Jesus sent disciples. Message is about mission and the importance of the relation between the one who send and the one who is sent. Sender gives full authority to the one who is sent. The one to be sent represents the sender in full scale. Jesus also commands to his disciples just before ascension: 'Go therefore and make disciples of all nations' (Mt. 28:19). This command of mission is passed over to members of WF through the disciples. WF is community to be sent to make disciples by God in and through Jesus Christ in this world, that is, in workplace. Being sent is an important theological perspective to have members of WF see their vocation with responsibility and faith. C. Sociological Reflection Korean war (1950-1953) had devastated Korean economy. Poverty was the main issue and problem to be solved to any subsequent political leaderships thereafter. Since 1962 Korean government launched a grand project called '5 Year Economic Development Plan.' The first '5 Year Economic Development Plan' was accomplished during 1962-1966 and the fifth and the last one during 1977-1981. 25 years of national project to elevate economic standard brought rapid and dramatic economic development and prosperity on the one hand, however, moral hazard and loss of ethics of work on the other hand resulting in the IMF period (1997-19998). WF understands their workplace as a mission field and vocation as place in and through which one is called to the service of God and the world. This kind of highly ethical and theological perception of vocation in the consciousness of members of WF came to be known and valued in and out of WF in this one-dimensional wasteland of this kingdom of profit. III. The Initial Stage of Workplace Faith Fellowship (1950s-1980s) A. Worship Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship 1. National Assembly Prayer Breakfast National Assembly Prayer Breakfast was begun in November 1965 by Christian members of the 6th National Assembly, led by Assemblywoman Hyun-Sook Park. The meeting was begun to better love brothers and sisters in Christ, to worship, and was started with the prayer that 'His will be done' in our nation 'as in Heaven.' In May of 1968, the National Assembly Prayer Breakfast and the Korean Prayer Breakfast Committees jointly established National Prayer Breakfast, an annual event where the President, prominent figures of the three departments of the government, and other leaders of different spheres of influence, gathered to pray. Those attending this Prayer Breakfast, despite their unique positions as members of the Assembly, approached the workplace with a firm sense of Christian duty, and the event sublimated into one in which true workplace worship occurred. Their main activity was their Prayer Breakfasts that were held on the first Wednesdays of each month at 7:30 am in the National Assembly Prayer Room (13206), during which the members held service and shared breakfast. They also held service on the days regular as well as extraordinary Assembly meetings were called to order. What is specially noteworthy is that even after the Christian members of the Assembly in opposing parties had confronted each other in fierce debates, they would always worship as one in Christ, giving honor to God and sharing love in fellowship with one another. 2. National Assembly Prayer Meetings National Assembly Prayer Meetings are a separate WF from National Assembly Breakfast Prayer. This WF had its start when three sisters in Christ (Kyung-Hae Kim, Young-Sook Choi, Chi-Myung Park) met to hold a prayer meeting on October 22, 1976. At the time, with no rooms available in which to have worship, the group of three met in storage rooms, ventilation room, or utility rooms to raise up earnest, tearful prayers. By God's provision they were able to hold their first meeting in their newly obtained permanent prayer room, in basement room 206, on September 12, 1979. The sound of prayer never ceased coming from this room for an entire year. On December 26 1979, the National Assembly Prayer Association's Inaugural General Synod (President: Chang-Lyul Kim) met, and on January 5th 1980 they held an Inaugural Worship Service Sermon: Bishop Gi-Chun Jang). B. Bible Study Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship As Bible study centered WF, Faith Movement for Bankers of the Bank of Korea can be pick up. It had its humble beginnings on August 27, 1975 with three people at the preparatory prayer meeting. On November 26 the same year, they had the Inaugural General Synod and began its growth as a WF. The regulation established at this time, 'We are to spread Biblically grounded Gospel, and in fostering interrelationship among members, give glory to God,' was the purpose of this ministry and now, 20 years after, the same holds. From March 20, 1978 four teams of 40 members committed to group Bible studies began. For those who may wonder, 'Why Bible studies at this particular time?', it could be said that the studies were prompted by the 'New Living' seminar that was started at Bank of We. At the time in 1978, over the course of four days of February 14th to the 17th at the 2nd meeting, an average of 350 people attended every day, making the Bank of Korea auditorium a place where many were touched. As an outflow of such memorable experience Bible study groups sprang up in different departments. As teaching material they used what Pastor Dong-Won Lee (Then Faith Movement for Bankers leader and Pastor of Global Missions Church) provided, 'The 9 Steps of the Creed.' The Bible studies span on average 30 to 40 minutes, and are divided into times of Bible study, prayer, fellowship, and praise. About 80% of the time is spent on the study of the Bible, which is also divided into Bible reading, teaching, and sharing, of which teaching is alloted 50% of the time. Outside the regular meetings, the Bible study members meet to visit and serve at centers for the disabled and senior citizens. They also collect money to celebrate special occasions such as birthdays and promotions, to give farewell gifts to those being transferred, and in addition, many groups jointly go on one day prayer retreats. C. Mission Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship The Missions Society of Seoul Bank is WF that was founded in the midst of much discord and hurt resulting from the merger between Seoul Bank and Sintak Bank in 1976. The group had its beginning as a seemingly inconsiderable prayer meeting. It was Jong-Bok Kim, then central staff member of CCC (Korea Campus Crusade for Christ)6), who had vision of having a group 'Centered ministering lay people at the workplace,' and to help foster the 'growth as a global bank' in order to 'share in the vision of world missions' which made the birth of this group, on January 1977, possible. In September of 1997, this small society grew to include 500 registered members with chapters in Busan, Jam-sil Jun-San Center, L.A., and developed to have different departments specializing in worship Service, evangelism, volunteering, pamphlet missions, and musical praise. To vitalize the regional chapters, advising pastors and/or officers are appointed to go and to take part in their worship services, partake in fellowship, and exchange information, particularly in order to discuss evangelism methods. Those from the main headquarters regularly attend meetings at the chapters and are jointly pushing for business missions. D. Fellowship-Diakonia Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship 1. Investment Firms Workplace Faith Fellowship At the starting point of the history of Korean WF, we find the Investment firm WF. On December 27; 1977, Christian employees working in investment firms with a united desire to spread the Gospel in their field established three independent WFs in the old National Theatre in Myoung Dong. The mission statement of the group was to foster the holy fellowship of believers in the realm of investment and to accomplish Jesus Christ's great missions commission. As they remained true to these founding principles and put them to action, the group now consists of 30 investment firms WFs with 3000 members spread over the country, including their four regional chapters in Busan, Gwang Joo, Ool San, and Dae Gu, and becomes an influential missions organization. 2. Youngrak Church's Workplace Church Worship Different from unit WFs with leadership taken by a particular WF and meeting held during the weekday, for workplace church worship type of WF, leadership is provided by the local church. This local church provides with leadership, fund, meeting place and other ones in need. This is immediately related to city church's mission strategy to reaching out surrounding regional community. This WP started by Youngnak Church (Senior Pastor: Chul-Shin Lee) located in Ju-Dong, Seoul, and also that first of its kind in Korea, celebrates its 35th anniversary in 2004. During lunch break of yet another ordinary Friday September 5th 1969, this kind of WF was offered to the workers in the area who were employed at places such as Ssang Young Cement, Bbaek General Hospital, and the Junbu Police Station. 10 people had attended the first worship service but at the present some 200 people have become regulars. E. Evaluation 1. Sociological and Theological Evaluation The economic state of Korea in its beginnings as a modern country was dismal. After the tragedy of the fratricidal Korean War, country faces a great hardship. Factories, buildings, railroads, and other facilities of value were all destroyed, and the toll on human life was tremendous. According to data from an organization, civilian casualties soared as high as 244, 663 for South Korea alone, higher for North Korea with 406,000 dead, with 303,212 missing, and 680,000 wounded or injured. No doubt, it was a period of great darkness. Notwithstanding, WF that was started in 1956 sublimated the deep hurts from the war with faith, and took on the great task of spreading the Gospel, and of serving society. When giving a theological (ecclesiological) evaluation of the WF in its early years, one should make it from the theological perspective of 'sending.' God is the subject of missions. God's mission began with the sending of His son Jesus Christ into this world, and the love that sent His only son was not limited to Israel or a certain nation but was meant for all of humanity. The theological perspective of 'sending' characterizes the nature of activities of WF in its initial stage of historical development. Also thanks to this theology the worship, service format centered on the leadership of minister gave way to that grounded upon the leadership of laity. This theology justifies the fact that worship could be brought out from the church building into the outside world. 2. Overall Evaluation It is worth noting that WF in its early stage was established out of the poor lay leaderships, inferior working environment in which general ethos is so opposite from that of Christian vision of living, and absence of more or less articulated theological ground. Namely, it would be likely that the most active minority are not in the mainstream in the workplace. This would probably result in WF's somewhat restricted influence on workplace or the society. Attempting to classify the various WFs from the early years, the writer suffers most because of rarity of materials answering questions like these: 'How many leaders were working?' 'how were they equipped with more technical knowledge,' 'how were new comers trained and nurtured?' 'how many people worked actively?' IV. E. Evaluation 1 Sociological and Theological Evaluation It would not be a stretch to say that phenomenal flourishing of Korea WFs in this middle period was a beneficiary of the impressive economic growth of the 1980s and 90s. After the Korean War, government adopted forceful economic policies, and accomplished amazing task which could be called 'the miracle of Han River.' Korea has been changed drastically from the agricultural nation to the highly developed industrial nation in this period. 2. General Evaluation WFs in this period were under the situation of astounding economic growth and development. It is to be noted, however, that economic growth brought about divisions and conflicts among the various groups of the economic classes. WF concerns this social conflicts in workplace. WFs were growing in number at this period. Yet along with this accomplishment we find that there are slight problems as well; surprisingly, there are no, and if any very few, cases of successful evangelization of non-believing co-workers in the company. It seems that the priorities had been shifted. It reminds me, as it is depicted in Acts 6:1-2, of how even those of the early church, after there was a great revival and masses became believers, found themselves in a situation where they were struggling with disunity in regards to relief work, as opposed to clinging harder to the most important things, that is, prayer and the Word: Now during those days, when the disciples were increasing in number, the Hellenists complained against the Hebrews because their widows were being neglected in the daily distribution of food. And the twelve called together the whole community of the disciples and said, 'It is not right that we should neglect the word of God in order to wait on tables.(Acts 6:1-2) Similarly we can see in this period that WFs put more emphasis on the derivative elements rather than on the most important, which was the saving of souls in the workplace. In addition, I would like to point out that much of missions of WF in the workplace was accomplished under the lay leadership, meaning that there decreased a feeling of necessity of the existence of the ordained ministry for the workplace and of the connection between WFs and local churches. Being a time of many shortcomings, this period was also a time during which companies of the faith were founded, and in which lay leadership in ministry is awakened and flourished. I would call this period as 'the Miracle of WF.' V. The Present Stage of the Workplace Faith Fellowship (1991-present) A. Worship Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship On October 12, 2003, the staff workers of True Love Haven Fire Kiln Sauna, Sung Joon Jung and his family, and employees at the Jung Gun Public Company gathered for their first worship service together. Fellowship-Diakonia Centered Workplace Faith Fellowship 1. E. Evaluation 1. Sociological and Theological Evaluation Korea in the 1990s used the authoritarian model of development and experienced an unrivaled growth rate which placed it on 11th place in the world as a powerful international trading country, and in 1995 the country entered into the age of 1 million dollar GNP (at the time it was 9,000,000 won), allowing them to become an OECD member in 1996, which all in turn, made this member of the Four Asian Dragons a subject of research as a model of 3rd world development. Yet on January 23, 1997, the bankruptcy of Han-Bo Steel Company and the downfall of foreign credit rating marked the beginning of a chain of events such as an insolvency postponement agreement, peace talks, court receivership, continued falling of stock and rising exchange rates, and the depletion of usable foreign currency reserves of the Korean bank, led to an official request to the IMF for a rescue loan on December 3, 1997, and as a result of the financial panic after the completion of the rescue loan agreement with the IMF, the economy recession worsened, leaving the country overall in a dire economic crisis. Yet despite the turbulence of going from one economic extreme to another, the National Christian Workplace Mission Council of the 90s, by continuing its organizational expansion into 31 regions to successfully form a national structure, showed a certain systemized strength. In fact, as the members of WFs played their part during the national crisis, the group showed its potential. In this crisis, theological implication of stewardship has played an important role to shape WF's self identity. 2. Overall Evaluation The Korean WFs of this period can be described with 'diversity,' in form as well as in workplaces in which they are founded. From the beginning of the late 90s, responding to what could fairly be termed as a new craze for workplace missions, new mission societies have been formed. The representative organization is the 'Korean Christian Workplace Mission Clergy Association ('KWC').' This association was founded on September 28, 1998 by the ministers of this country's mainstream denominations. KWC and 'Korean Christian Workplace Mission Association,' sharing the same office, expressing their cooperation for mission, still have fundamental differences in the makeup one is for pastors, and the other for laity. The forming of the KWC suggests in some way that the clergy are actively entering into workplace missions. Another problem is the inferior research situation. There is a lack of interest among churches, denominations, seminaries and ministers in this field, not to mention research. This situation is reflected on the publication of books on this subject. Hong-Il Park's book, Workplace Missions and Site of Life was published on February of 2000, and Theology of Mission in Workplace,' authored by Kyung Won Kim, Dong Yoon Jun, and Sang Gi Jun, was published as late as September of 2001. Needless to say, there is an extreme lack of dissertations and research work as well as educational material written on this topic. Within the church, too, education provided for workers is not readily available, not continuous, or systematized. Yet devotion and effort shown by the various WFs deserve acknowledgement and compliments. It is my analysis that these WFs provided great encouragement to Korean workers and Korean citizens overall who were suffering under unprecedented national hardship during IMF period. VI. Conclusion Questions driving the writer last ten year in his double ministries both in the local church and workplace setting are like these: 'Why am I so eagerly involved in the ministry for the workplace along with the ministry for local church?'; 'How could the 'AT help members living faithfully their Christian life in the real life of the workplace?' The writer has revealed, analyzed and evaluated the activities and influence of the WF in four typologies following three stages of historical development with sociological and theological perspective in view. And the thesis intends to be an answer to those questions. One of recent statistics shows that many of workers aged twenty to thirty supposed to be dressed up with excitement and vision, however, feel unsecured in their workplace owing to the threatening situation of economic depression in the larger context and discharge in the small context. It is a symbolic indication of the hard reality of life condition to get through in Korea. Workplace is the one in which the secular and Christian faith is clashed, Christian faith is supposed to take reality, and, the meaning of faith continued to be questioned and deepened in concrete way. WF is the community gathered in the name of Jesus Christ right in this heart of secular section, based on the biblical phrase: 'Where two or three are gathered in my name, I am there among them' (Mt. 18:20), thereby witnessing Lord's presence and its salvafic implications for the people's lives in the workplace. It has been the place in which workers of Christian faith is given hope, encouragement and calling experience. Especially calling experience such that God works through me in this place or God brought me here appears to be the background of ethical and spiritual reading of secular vocation and workplace. It has been the place in which all the Christian members are brought and transfigured into one body of Christ, sharing brotherhood and sisterhood, and, breaking sorrow and joy of life together. Study characterizes WF as a source of spiritual power to help members overcoming duality of faith and life, family and workplace, worship and secular vocation to the maturity of more comprehensive Christian life, defining those effects an important contribution WF made for the Korean church and society. Thesis characterizes activities of WF in four typologies of the worship-centered, the Bible study-centered, mission-centered, and fellowship-centered, and, evaluates each typology from theological and sociological dimension with historical background in view. In chapter II, the writer presents theoretical ground of WF in terms of its historical, theological, and, sociological aspect. Historically, three types of WF were introduced. They are categorized by the nature of leadership: 'Independent WF,' the first Christian meeting held in workplace, 'Workplace Mission Association,' and 'Work Place Church Worship.' Theologically the self identity and activities of these groups in the early stage reflect theology of laity nurtured by the doctrine of priesthood of believers, devotional stewardship, and missiological vision Jesus exemplified in his training and sending of disciples. Sociologically, the writer shows how theses groups adapt themselves in the rapid societal change during 25 years of 'The Five Year Economic Development Plan' designed and led by government. In chapter III, the writer deals with the period beginning from the time of establishment of 'Korean WF' ending up to 1980 when the sequence of several '5 Year Economic Development Project' was closed. Groups are categorized in four and evaluated in its theological and sociological aspect: Worship Centered WF (Congressman's Breakfast Prayer Meeting-1965, Congress Prayer Meeting-1976) Bible Study Centered WF (Korean Bank Mission-1975) Mission Centered WF (Seoul Bank Mission-1977) Fellowship and Social Service Centered WF (Stock Committee Mission-1977). It is evident that groups of this period especially refer to theology of sending for their self identity. In chapter IV, the writer presents several groups belonging to the middle stage covering from 1980 to 1990. WFs in Korea reaches its golden age with the emergence of 'Christian Work Place Mission Council.' Groups are categorized in four and evaluated in its theological and sociological aspect: Worship Centered WF (Sacred Love Church Furniture-1984, Ebenesel WF-1984, Seoul Metropolitan Subway Co. WF-1984), Bible Study Centered WF ('BBB' meaning Business Bible Belt), Mission Centered WF which shows new pattern of workplace mission (City of Incheon WF Association-1988, City of Yeosou WF Association-1984, City of Daegu and Kyoungbuk WF Association-1990, City of Chuncheon WF Association-1990, City of Ulgin Nuclear Power Station WF-1985), Fellowship and Social Service Centered WF (Korean Electronic Co. WF-1989, Korean Drivers' Association-1985). Their activities appears to be grounded upon the theology of laity. In chapter V, the writer presents relatively recent activities of WF. After several decades of individual or corporative activities of WF, there established a 'Korean WF Mission General Council' for more mutual encouragement, exchange of information, and effective mission task. It was remarkable event in the history of workplace mission in Korea. Furthermore this insitution was registered as a corporation aggregate in the Ministry of Culture & Tourism. Groups are categorized in four and evaluated in its theological and sociological aspect: Worship Centered WF (True Love Shelter-2003), Bible Study Centered WFs which use Bible study text produced by NLTC (New Life Training Camp), Mission Centered WF (Korean Government Employee WF Association-1998, Ministry of Finance and Economy WF Association-1994), and, Fellowship and Social Service Centered WF (Korean Correctional Institution WF Association-1992). Their activities appears to be grounded upon the theology of stewardship. The writer attempts to introduce the hidden activities and stories of WF which has exercised positive influence on all sides of lives of Christian families, churches in Korea and of Korean society. They worked voluntarily with resolution. They lighted a candle of love in the darkness of workplace where competition, conspiracy, and hatred predominates, and, proclaimed the Sacred in the cement buildings of modern secular cities. To reveal their devotion, activities and theology itself would be a contribution to Korean churches in general. Churches always emphasize living worship, but not provides structures and leadership for living worship. All kinds of WF function to bridge church and life. Study attempts to cover all kinds of WF activities in full scale. But it was not easy to get all the official informations from WF. WF did not have an office to store the documents nor payed administrative leadership. Making and storing documents were not their primary concern. There might be still so many groups in workplace whose activities are not captured within writer's view. That might be the limit of the study. But if there is still something consoling the writer, it is the fact that there has been not one attempt to categorize WF movement periodically and typologically and to evaluate it with historical, theological, and sociological perspective.
author: 이성원

title: Big data, oriented-organizational culture, and business performance: A socio-technical approach
abstract: This paper experimentally examines the impact of oriented-organizational culture that could support big data analytics (BDA) in higher education institutions (HEIs) in Saudi Arabia. Specifically, this study analyzed the effect of oriented-organizational culture (OC) on big data tasks (BDTs) toward improving decision-making (DM) and organization performance (OP). The study hinged on the theory of socio-technical systems to investigate BDA elements in higher education decision-making in Saudi Arabia. The analysis was conducted using a quantitative survey research design where data were collected from 270 IT staff working in Saudi Arabian HEIs using Qualtrics. PLS-SEM was applied to validate the research data and explore the relationship between the proposed hypotheses. The findings show that oriented-organizational culture positively affected big data tasks, i.e., storing, analyzing, and visualizing. Similarly, oriented-organizational culture positively affects improving decision-making by top management in Saudi Arabian universities. OC also positively influences the performance of Saudi Arabian universities. Improving decision-making by top management has a positive impact on enhancing the overall university’s performance. However, big data tasks, i.e., storing, analyzing, and visualizing, negatively affect improving decision-making by top management in Saudi Arabian HEIs. One of the study limitations is the small sample size; future studies should include private and public universities to alter the expected outcomes. Additional technological elements, such as IT infrastructure at Saudi Arabia’s private and public HEIs, are recommended to be considered in future studies to establish the competence of respective IT infrastructure. AcknowledgmentThe authors wish to thank the Problems and Perspectives in Management Journal editors for their valuable time and assistance in improving the manuscript.
author: Aseeri, Maher;Kang, Kyeong;

title: Socio-technical factors influencing big data analytics adoption in healthcare
abstract: The purpose of this study is to determine the key socio-technical factors influencing big data analytics adoption in healthcare services. A systematic literature review was conducted using peer-reviewed scholarly publications spanning from 2013 to 2023 to illuminate the influencing factors. Twelve papers focused on the factors influencing big data analytics (BDA) adoption in healthcare services were included for review. The factors were divided into four major groups namely i) person, ii) technology, iii) organization, and iv) environment. Analytical skills define a person, whereas technology is characterized by system quality and information quality. Organization support, organization resources, training, data governance, and evidence-based decision-making are all associated with the organization. Finally, government regulations are allocated to the environment. This review presents evidence of the socio-technical factors that influence big data analytics adoption in healthcare services. The findings from this review recommend future big data analytics adoption in healthcare services to carefully evaluate the factors identified in this study.
author: Wolseley, Nik Nurdini;Salahuddin, Lizawati;Mohd Aboobaider, Burhanuddin;Raja Ikram, Raja Rina;Hashim, Ummi Rabaah;Abdul Rahim, Fiza;

title: Big data analytics on large-scale socio-technical software engineering archives
abstract: Given the fast growing nature of software engineering data in online software repositories and open source communities, it would be helpful to analyse these assets to discover valuable information about the software engineering development process and other related data. Big Data Analytics (BDA) techniques and frameworks can be applied on these data resources to achieve a high-performance and relevant data collection and analysis. Software engineering is a socio-technical process which needs development team collaboration and technical knowledge to develop a high-quality application. GitHub, as an online social coding foundation, contains valuable information about the software engineers' communications and project life cycles. In this paper, unsupervised data mining techniques are applied on the data collected by general Big Data approaches to analyse GitHub projects, source codes and interactions. Source codes and projects are clustered using features and metrics derived from historical data in repositories, object oriented programming metrics and the influences of developers on source codes.
